question: Can I do Deliveroo or Uber Eats shifts on a Student visa?
expected_location: What you can and cannot do|ST 26.5|Student and Child Student: Prohibited work;Work Conditions for a Student|Work conditions
reference_answer: It depends on how the work is set up. On a Student visa you can't be self-employed, so you can't do delivery shifts as a self-employed or freelance rider. If the role is a job where the company employs you, it's allowed within your normal work limits: up to 20 hours a week during term time if you're studying at degree level at a university (10 hours if your course is below degree level), and full-time outside term time. The rules don't say whether delivery app riders count as employed or self-employed, so check your contract before you start. If it treats you as self-employed, you can't take the work.

question: I saw reports that students who applied between 2023 and 2026 might get part of their visa fee back. Is that real, and do I need to claim it?
reference_answer: I can't confirm that from the guidance I have. It doesn't mention any partial refund of Student visa fees for people who applied between 2023 and 2026, so I can't tell you whether the reports are accurate, whether you'd qualify, or whether you'd need to claim. The only refunds it mentions are for withdrawn applications and a health surcharge refund for people working in public-sector healthcare, and neither of those is the refund in the reports. To check, look for an official Home Office announcement on GOV.UK, or ask your university's international student advice team, who can tell you whether anything has been confirmed and how to claim.
